general_background.title: Octadecene is not always inert
general_background.summary: Octadecene provides a weakly coordinating medium for hot solution growth, leaving the ligands more freedom to control surface binding. It can also polymerize under growth conditions, leaving an alkene-derived residue that is difficult to separate from hydrophobic nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Oleate and the nanocrystal surface
general_background.summary: Bound oleate can stabilize dispersed metal chalcogenide nanocrystals, and not all surface carboxylate need occupy the same binding environment. Displacing metal carboxylate from the surface can change surface stoichiometry as well as colloidal stability.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Ligand Exchange and the Stoichiometry of Metal Chalcogenide Nanocrystals: Spectroscopic Observation of Facile Metal-Carboxylate Displacement and Binding

general_background.title: Ligand exchange can alter surface stoichiometry
general_background.summary: A neutral donor is an L-type ligand, an anionic ligand can be X-type, and a surface-bound Lewis acid can act as Z-type. Displacing a Lewis-acidic metal carboxylate during ligand exchange can change surface stoichiometry as well as the coating.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Nucleation and size focusing
general_background.summary: A rapid change in precursor availability can create a short nucleation period followed by growth on existing particles. Growth can narrow the size distribution while material is supplied, whereas later ripening can consume smaller particles and change that distribution again.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
